repetition

/rep-uh-TISH-un/ — rhymes with nutrition · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Repetition is the act of doing or saying again something that has already occurred.

She insisted that only through this steady repetition would the movements sink into my hands so deeply that I would no longer have to think about them.

Worked Example

The old song played in the grocery store—the same verse, the same chorus, repeating four times before the song ended—making her hum it for hours afterward.

Repetition is more precise than 'repeating' or 'repetitiveness' because it is the noun form that names the act itself as a thing, a technique, something that can be used intentionally. In this song context, the repetition is what makes the tune stick.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

iteration: An iteration is one pass through a repeating process, and each pass may differ from the last — software improves iteration by iteration. Repetition is the act of doing the same thing again, with sameness at its core. An iteration moves a cycle forward; a repetition circles back to do the identical thing once more.

recurrence: A recurrence is a single instance of something coming back, often unplanned and unwelcome — a recurrence of an illness, of flooding. Repetition is the deliberate or ongoing act of doing or saying a thing again. A patient dreads a recurrence; an actor rehearsing lines depends on repetition.

replication: Replication means producing an exact copy — scientists replicate experiments, machines replicate parts. Repetition means performing an action again, whether or not anything identical is produced. You replicate a result; you repeat a drill. Replication is about the copy; repetition is about the doing-again.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

originality: creating something new instead of repeating

variation: deliberately changing something with each pass

Where it sits · how many times it happens — once → again → repeatedly → repetition

once vs. repetition: Proofreading an essay once will catch a few errors, but once names a single pass — far weaker than repetition, the act of going back through again and again until the text is clean.

again vs. repetition: Knocking on the door again means just one more knock; again points to a single extra instance, while repetition names an ongoing series of the same act.

repeatedly vs. repetition: A commuter who repeatedly misses the bus does the same thing many times, but repeatedly is only an adverb describing how something happens; repetition is the stronger noun that names the act itself — a tool a teacher or poet can deliberately use.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again, back

Root — pet-

Root — pet-: to seek, go toward, rush at (from Latin petere)

Suffix — -ition

Suffix — -ition: act or state of (noun-forming)

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (again) + pet- (to seek, go toward) + -ition (act of) builds the meaning piece by piece: the act of going after something again — doing or saying it over and over. The suffix -ition is what turns the action into a thing you can name: repeat the action, and the repetition is the result. Keep an eye on pet-: it is a busy Latin root, and you will meet it again in this unit.

Use the root in a new word: petition

Use the root in a new word: petition: The residents filed a petition with the city council, requesting that the park be kept open another year.

Word Choice

neutral

Repetition is a straightforward, everyday word that can be used in positive contexts (learning through repetition) or negative ones (the repetition gets boring). When you need to emphasize doing something again and again—whether for learning, practice, or effect—repetition is your word. For a single instance of something happening again, 'recurrence' is better; for the idea of repeating a pattern, 'pattern' might be simpler.
